title: UPDATE: Figure Launches Hark Pro with 100,000 Free Paid Plans
summary:
General access to the newest proactive AI tool from Figure is now open on mobile and web platforms, transitioning the product from a closed waitlist. The release of Hark Pro includes a promotion giving the first 100,000 sign-ups a paid plan for free, while founder Brett Adcock provided the first month of the $100 Pro plan to early users through October 6. The interface includes a feature called Handoff, a private virtual computer that design head Abidur Chowdhury describes as an "operating system for your life."

Figure has raised $700M at a $6B valuation to develop its proactive AI ecosystem. Its Handoff tool recorded a 97.7 score on the Online-Mind2Web web-agent benchmark, surpassing the 92.8 score of GPT 5.4 and the 84.1 score of Claude Opus 4.8. The assistant integrates multiple AI models to handle widgets, chats, and scheduled tasks across Android, iOS, and web browsers.

selectedTweets.text:
100,000 free paid plans.

That is how Brett Adcock is launching Hark this week. The founder @adcock_brett announced on X: the first 100,000 sign-ups get the paid plan free.

Not free for a while. A hard cap. That turns a launch announcement into a race, and everyone who misses the cap becomes the next wave of demand.

The product backs the pitch. Hark Handoff scores 97.7 on the Online-Mind2Web web-agent benchmark, ahead of GPT 5.4 at 92.8 and Claude Opus 4.8 at 84.1.

$700M raised at a $6B valuation, and the whole launch is one post with a number in it.

Steal this: if your launch offer has no cap and no deadline, it is not an offer. It is a pricing page.

selectedTweets.text:
I'm very intrigued by @hark_labs Pro and its private virtual computer Handoff. The AI startup just unveiled the UI for the "operating system for your life." 

I chatted with Abidur Chowdhury, head of design, and he did a few demos of the UI for me. You may remember him as the guy who introduced the iPhone Air in September 2025 and then left two months later and surfaced at Hark

The interface looks very promising, very Apple, very zen. 

He didn't mince words:

“I don't really want to go look at 10 shitty websites and different dentists in my local area and make sure that they all have time available before I'm ready at work. And then the websites are not optimized for looking through really quickly,” Chowdhury said.

Instead, just let Hark do the shit for you

NGL, I haven't felt this feeling since @joshm put me onto Arc browser

https://t.co/YM2pRF9KgO
